scenes.credit: a sketch generated for the article

steps.say: A photographed sketch of a room. No source file. Somebody has to redraw it in AutoCAD, one line at a time.

scenes.headline: How an agent skill redraws a sketch as DWG
scenes.sub: pengxiaoan's autocad-dwg-redraw-skill, read file by file
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Burl! This open skill promises to do it for you, and to say which numbers it guessed. I read every file.

steps.say: First, a quick check of the image: size, blur and contrast.

steps.term: Spec: the drawing as JSON entities
steps.say: Then the key step, and no script does it. The model looks at the picture and types the drawing as JSON.
A validator checks the JSON's shape.
Python drives AutoCAD over COM, one call per entity, and saves a DWG.
A preview is rendered on a fixed page.
Then the preview is laid over the source, to measure how far apart the lines are.

scenes.credit: the repository's example spec, drawn for the article
scenes.title: Every value carries a tag

steps.say: Here is the one worked example in the repository. Five entities on a small part.

steps.caption: known, scaled, inferred, unreadable
steps.say: Each value says where it came from. Read off the drawing, scaled from pixels, inferred, or unreadable.

scenes.title: Four colours, four kinds of number

params.drawn: In the DWG, the tags are gone

steps.say: Take a small plan. The model redraws the walls and types every dimension.
Two are printed on the sketch. Six thousand, and two thousand four hundred. Those are known.

steps.term: Anchor: a known length used to set the scale
steps.say: The rest are measured in pixels and scaled by an anchor, the nine hundred pixel overall width.
The door is a guess at a standard size. The window's label is smudged, so it stays unreadable.
Now misplace one end of the anchor by four pixels. The wall becomes three thousand five hundred and eighty-four, and the chain stops adding up.
That ledger is the right idea. But the drawing script never reads it. In the DWG, every dimension looks the same.

scenes.title: Why one bad anchor costs so much

parts.note: pixels off at one end of the anchor
parts.say: The slip is how far off one endpoint is, in pixels.
The span is how long the anchor is. A four pixel slip on nine hundred is about zero point four four percent.
Every scaled length shares it. On a sixty pixel column, the same slip is six point two five percent.

scenes.title: One bad click on the anchor

steps.caption: a 4 px slip on the 900 px anchor
steps.say: Here it is in the article's own widget. Slip the anchor by four pixels, and the scaled values drift while the chain check turns red.

steps.caption: the short column anchor
steps.say: Calibrate on the short column instead, and the same slip throws every scaled length much further.

steps.caption: the DWG as drawn
steps.say: Then look at the drawing AutoCAD gets. The colours are gone. Nothing in the file says which numbers were guessed.

scenes.credit: the article's reimplementation of the comparison
scenes.title: What the comparison can see

steps.caption: red: source edges, blue: redraw
steps.say: The check fits the redraw onto the sketch at four corners, then measures edge distances. An exact redraw sits right on top.

steps.caption: every length 3% too long
steps.say: Now make every length three percent too long. After the corner fit, it scores exactly like the perfect one.

steps.caption: interior wall 300 mm off: p95 38.2 px
steps.say: A wall in the wrong place does show. The ninety-fifth percentile jumps to thirty-eight pixels.

steps.caption: door missing: only source to CAD sees it
steps.say: A missing door shows only one way round, from the sketch to the redraw.

scenes.quote: assess registered visual linework, not physical dimensions or units
scenes.say: Its own warning says the metrics assess registered visual linework, not physical dimensions or units. And the status it writes is always pass.

scenes.title: The post's seven claims, against the code

states.say: Two hold as written: the drawing data, and AutoCAD drawing it. Five hold in part. Recognition is the model's, and the ledger stays in the JSON.

items.text: Carry the tag on the element
items.say: For drawings to BIM, keep the tag on the element, so it survives the file.

items.text: Diff every view against its sheet
items.say: Diff every view against its sheet. It catches a wall on the wrong grid line.
And check the scale against printed dimension chains, because the diff cannot.

scenes.text: Tag every number by where it came from, and never let a picture that looks right stand in for a dimension.
scenes.mark: Tag every number by where it came from
scenes.say: Read it as a specification. Tag every number by where it came from, and never let a picture that looks right stand in for a dimension.
